# STM32H743 AIO Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC: Power, Thermal, and DShot Architecture

**Scope note.** I don't have the Job #41 BOM, stackup, or layout. Every parameter below is a stated assumption: substitute your datasheet values into the equations. The architectural conclusions hold across reasonable part choices. The numeric results are only as good as the inputs.

**One architectural clarification first.** In an AIO design, the STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and emits DShot. The 48 kHz PWM and commutation are generated by the ESC-side MCUs (for example AT32F421 or EFM8 running AM32 or BLHeli_32), not by the H743. The two domains are modelled separately below.

---

## 1. Design Assumptions

| Parameter | Symbol | Assumed value |
|---|---|---|
| Battery | V_bus | 6S, 25.2 V max / 22.2 V nominal |
| Burst phase current per ESC | I_ph | 80 A |
| PWM frequency | f_sw | 48 kHz, complementary (synchronous rectification) |
| MOSFET | — | 40 V N-ch, 3.3×3.3 DFN, R_DS(on),25 = 1.2 mΩ @ V_GS = 10 V |
| R_DS(on) tempco | α | ≈ 0.4 %/°C (≈1.3× at 100 °C) |
| Gate charges | Q_g / Q_gs2 / Q_gd | 30 / 4 / 6 nC |
| Reverse recovery / output charge | Q_rr / Q_oss | 30 nC / 20 nC |
| Body diode V_f | V_f | 0.8 V |
| Dead time | t_d | 50 ns per edge |
| Gate drive | V_drv, R_g,total | 10 V, 6 Ω (5 Ω ext + 1 Ω int) |
| Miller plateau | V_pl | 3 V |
| PCB copper path (bus + phase, per conducting path) | R_cu | 0.6 mΩ |
| Board | — | 25.5×25.5 mm, 1.6 mm, 6-layer, 2 oz all layers |

**Margin warning.** 40 V FETs on 6S leave about 15 V of headroom for regen spikes and L·di/dt ringing. That is acceptable only with low-ESR bulk capacitance at the board input (≥1000 µF low-ESR, plus a TVS). Otherwise consider 60 V parts and accept roughly 1.5–2× higher R_DS(on).

---

## 2. Conduction Loss Model

### 2.1 Temperature-dependent resistance

$$R_{DS}(T_j) = R_{DS,25}\,[1 + \alpha (T_j - 25)]$$

At T_j = 100 °C: R_DS = 1.2 × 1.30 = **1.56 mΩ**

### 2.2 Path topology (6-step trapezoidal, complementary PWM)

At any instant, current flows through one high-side and one low-side position of two legs. Within the PWM leg, the HS FET and the synchronous LS FET split the period as D and (1−D). Their duty cycles sum to 1, so the I² loss is duty-independent to first order:

$$P_{cond,ESC} = 2\,I_{ph}^2\,R_{DS}(T_j) + I_{ph}^2 R_{cu}$$

$$P_{cond,ESC} = 2(6400)(1.56\text{e-}3) + 6400(0.6\text{e-}3) = 19.97 + 3.84 = \mathbf{23.8\ W}$$

For FOC/sinusoidal drive, replace I_ph with I_rms and use 3 FET-equivalents weighted by modulation. The result is within about 10 % for this estimate.
